title: Manager Ross steals the money and Phillips quits in Charlotte
summary: Phillips says the booking manager Ross and singer Billy Coleman skimmed ticket money, so he and several others quit King Oliver's band in Charlotte, North Carolina.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x:
couple of cars, a truck, or something like that...
Then, see, the reason we left the band was on account of Ross. He was stealing all the money. I knew he was stealing. We just said, "Man, we ain't goin' no further." He was handling the band. He would say it didn't make nothin'. Then he and Billy Coleman, they would work together... Billy sometimes worked on the door taking up tickets. He and the doorman would get together on the door, and they would sell so many tickets for themselves. So they caught up with him and got rid of him, because he wasn't no good to the band. They were going to let him go anyway. He was supposed to have been a singer or something. But he wasn't nothin'.
Was he the guy who used to sometimes take off without getting permission? Not show up or something? Or was that somebody else? Somebody used to take a leave of absence without getting permission.
You mean with King?
Yeah.

Well... I can't remember when that was... No, wouldn't nobody have missed him no way. He wasn't doin' nothin'. He'd go up there and try to sing and do a comedy act. It really wasn't no act. They hired him for singing, and he'd come up there doing Stepin Fetchit. That kind of stuff. So anyway, then he started stealing that money. He would get to go in town, and there was the tickets and things
Phillips - 163

for the dance, he and the man that owned the hall would get together. But one man didn't get together, and he came back and told King about what he wanted him to do. So we got rid of him. We left him right in that town, and went on from there.
Anyway, then Ross, he was taking money. So we just quit. We quit. I said, "Man, I ain't going no further." So Sam said he wasn't going, and quit. Charlie, Debo and Dan...
Dan Andrews.
Yeah. Dan didn't go with us, though.
What city did you quit in?
We quit in Charlotte, North Carolina. I don't think that said that, though.
I think this said you left in Knoxville.
It was Charlotte.
[PAUSE; TELEPHONE]
You were talking about leaving the band, and you said it was in Charlotte, not in Knoxville.
It was Charlotte.
Who was it again who left in Charlotte, and who was there after you had gone?
Pete Jones stayed there. Selmer Payne and Bernie Cobb.
And who left?
Whitby and Sam Allen and myself, Red, Debo,
Phillips - 164
Charlie Toran and Duff. So we had a job to go to in Portsmouth, Ohio. We went back to Portsmouth.
